threatContext.unauthorized-access: Firebase Security Rules set to allow read/write true granting public database access, Firestore rules not validating request.auth causing unauthenticated data access, Storage bucket rules allowing anonymous file uploads, REST API access bypassing client SDK rule enforcement
threatContext.misconfiguration: Realtime Database rules set to '.read: true, .write: true' exposing all data, Firestore rules with overly broad wildcard matches, Firebase project API keys exposed (not restricted to specific APIs), App Check not enforced allowing direct API abuse, Cloud Functions deployed without authentication requirements
threatContext.sensitive-data-exposure: Firebase config object (apiKey, authDomain, databaseURL) exposed in client-side JavaScript, user PII stored in Realtime Database accessible via REST API, Firestore documents containing sensitive data without field-level security rules, Firebase Analytics collecting user data without consent controls
threatContext.data-exfiltration: Realtime Database full export via REST API (/.json endpoint), Firestore collection group queries extracting data across subcollections, Firebase Storage bucket enumeration and bulk download, Cloud Functions used as data proxy to exfiltrate to external endpoints
threatContext.broken-authentication: Firebase Authentication email enumeration via fetchSignInMethodsForEmail, weak password requirements in email/password provider, custom token generation with insufficient validation, anonymous authentication upgrade attacks, OAuth provider misconfiguration allowing account takeover via unverified email claims

nosql-injection: Validate and sanitize all client-side query parameters before constructing Firestore or Realtime Database queries
Use Firebase Security Rules to enforce data type validation and reject malformed inputs at the database level
Avoid constructing dynamic database references from user input; use parameterized queries in Cloud Functions
Enable Firebase App Check to ensure only verified app instances can access your database APIs
unauthorized-access: Write restrictive Firebase Security Rules that validate request.auth on all read and write operations
Enable Firebase App Check with reCAPTCHA Enterprise or DeviceCheck to prevent direct REST API abuse
Use custom claims in Firebase Auth tokens to implement role-based access control in Security Rules
Restrict Firebase Storage bucket rules to authenticated users with specific custom claim requirements
misconfiguration: Replace default Realtime Database rules (.read: true, .write: true) with restrictive per-path rules before deployment
Use Firebase Emulator Suite to test Security Rules locally before deploying to production
Restrict Firebase API keys to specific APIs (Auth, Firestore, Storage) using Google Cloud Console API key restrictions
Enforce Firebase App Check on all services (Firestore, Realtime Database, Storage, Cloud Functions) in production
sensitive-data-exposure: Restrict Firebase config exposure by using API key restrictions in Google Cloud Console to limit key usage to specific domains and APIs
Implement field-level Security Rules in Firestore to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive document fields
Configure Firebase Analytics data retention settings and disable collection of user-level PII where not required
Use server-side Cloud Functions for sensitive data operations rather than direct client-side database access
data-exfiltration: Implement Security Rules that limit query result sizes and prevent full-collection reads (e.g., require filters on indexed fields)
Disable the Realtime Database REST API (/.json endpoint) or restrict it with Security Rules requiring authentication
Use Firebase Storage Security Rules to prevent unauthenticated bucket listing and bulk file downloads
Monitor Firebase Usage dashboard and set budget alerts to detect unusual read/download spikes indicating data extraction
broken-authentication: Disable fetchSignInMethodsForEmail API to prevent email enumeration (enable Email Enumeration Protection in Firebase Auth settings)
Configure strong password requirements in Firebase Auth settings (minimum length, complexity)
Require email verification before granting access to protected resources via Security Rules checking request.auth.token.email_verified
Review OAuth provider configurations and enforce email verification for social sign-in providers to prevent account takeover via unverified email claims

services.name: Supabase
services.description: Open-source Firebase alternative with PostgreSQL database, auth, and APIs

threatContext.sql-injection: Direct PostgreSQL access via exposed connection strings, SQL injection through PostgREST API filters (e.g., crafted .or()/.filter() parameters), raw SQL execution in Edge Functions or server-side clients bypassing parameterization, RPC function calls with unsanitized inputs
threatContext.unauthorized-access: Anon key abuse to access unprotected tables without RLS, service_role key exposure granting full database bypass of Row Level Security, PostgREST API enumeration of tables and columns via OpenAPI schema, JWT forgery if JWT secret is leaked from project settings
threatContext.misconfiguration: Row Level Security (RLS) not enabled on tables leaving data publicly accessible via anon key, overly permissive RLS policies using auth.role() = 'authenticated' without user-specific checks, Storage buckets set to public allowing unauthenticated file access, service_role key used in client-side code, Realtime subscriptions enabled on sensitive tables without RLS
threatContext.sensitive-data-exposure: PostgREST API auto-exposing all columns in public schema tables, Realtime subscriptions broadcasting row changes including sensitive fields to subscribed clients, auth.users table metadata leakage via admin API, Storage object metadata and signed URLs exposing file contents, database connection strings in client-side environment variables
threatContext.data-exfiltration: Bulk data extraction via PostgREST API with permissive RLS or no RLS (SELECT * without pagination limits), Storage bucket enumeration and mass file download, database dumps via exposed direct PostgreSQL connection strings, Realtime change feed capture for continuous data siphoning, pg_dump execution through compromised service_role credentials
threatContext.broken-authentication: Auth provider misconfiguration allowing OAuth account linking without email verification, JWT secret exposure enabling token forgery, email enumeration via sign-up and password reset endpoints, weak password policies in email/password auth, magic link token interception, disabled email confirmation allowing immediate account access

sql-injection: Use Supabase client library parameterized queries (.eq(), .in(), .filter()) rather than raw SQL for all user-facing operations
Avoid exposing raw SQL execution via RPC functions to untrusted inputs; validate and sanitize all RPC parameters
Use PostgreSQL prepared statements in Edge Functions and server-side clients to prevent SQL injection
Restrict the PostgREST API to specific schemas and tables using Supabase's API settings rather than exposing the full public schema
unauthorized-access: Enable Row Level Security (RLS) on all tables in Supabase and write policies that check auth.uid() for user-specific access
Never expose the service_role key in client-side code; use the anon key with RLS policies for all browser-based operations
Restrict Supabase project JWT secret access and rotate it if exposed to prevent JWT forgery
Disable the OpenAPI schema endpoint or restrict it to authenticated users to prevent table and column enumeration
misconfiguration: Enable RLS on every table and verify policies with Supabase's RLS debugger before exposing tables via the API
Set Storage buckets to private by default and create specific RLS policies for file access
Disable Realtime subscriptions on sensitive tables or enforce RLS on Realtime channels in Supabase project settings
Use Supabase environment variables correctly: never put service_role key in NEXT_PUBLIC_ or client-accessible variables
sensitive-data-exposure: Use PostgREST column-level grants to restrict which columns are exposed via the auto-generated API
Configure Realtime subscription filters to prevent broadcasting sensitive row data to unauthorized subscribers
Restrict Supabase Auth admin API access and avoid exposing auth.users table data through custom API endpoints
Use Supabase Vault to store and manage secrets rather than storing them in database tables
data-exfiltration: Implement RLS policies with row-count limits and require pagination to prevent bulk data extraction via the PostgREST API
Restrict direct PostgreSQL connection string access to server-side services only and disable pooler access from untrusted networks
Use Supabase Storage RLS policies to prevent anonymous bucket listing and mass file downloads
Monitor Supabase project logs and database query patterns for unusual SELECT volumes or pg_dump activity
broken-authentication: Enable email confirmation for all sign-up flows in Supabase Auth settings to prevent immediate unauthorized access
Configure strong password requirements (minimum length, complexity) in Supabase Auth settings
Require email verification for OAuth providers and prevent account linking with unverified email addresses
Restrict magic link and OTP token validity periods to short durations and enable rate limiting on auth endpoints

services.name: OpenAI API
services.description: Third-party hosted LLM API (GPT models) consumed over the internet

threatContext.prompt-injection: Direct jailbreaks against /v1/chat/completions and /v1/responses, indirect prompt injection from retrieved documents or web content fed into context, system prompt override and extraction, malicious instructions in tool/function-call results steering subsequent model actions
threatContext.sensitive-data-exposure: PII, secrets, and proprietary source code embedded in prompts and sent to OpenAI, sensitive data returned in completions and logged application-side, conversation and file content retained by the provider outside the org boundary unless zero-retention is negotiated
threatContext.saas-data-leakage: Regulated or confidential data leaving the organisation in prompts, embeddings, or fine-tuning datasets uploaded to the Files API, use of consumer ChatGPT accounts instead of the enterprise API for corporate data
threatContext.credential-theft: OpenAI API keys (sk-...) leaked in client-side code, mobile apps, public git repos, or CI logs, project/service-account keys with organisation-wide scope reused across services, keys embedded in browser-exposed frontends
threatContext.excessive-permissions: Function/tool definitions exposing high-privilege actions (database writes, shell, payment APIs) that the model can invoke autonomously, agentic tool-calling loops acting without human confirmation, overly broad function schemas
threatContext.injection-attack: Insecure output handling where model responses are rendered as HTML/Markdown (stored XSS), passed to eval/exec, used to build SQL, or written to shell commands without validation (OWASP LLM02)
threatContext.third-party-integration-risk: Dependence on a single external provider for availability and confidentiality, provider-side breaches or model changes affecting the application, plugins/Actions and Assistants tools reaching internal systems

prompt-injection: Treat all model input as untrusted: isolate system instructions from user and retrieved content, and never concatenate untrusted documents directly into the system prompt
Require human-in-the-loop confirmation for any tool/function call that performs state-changing or high-impact actions
Apply input/output guardrails (e.g., a moderation pass or a dedicated classifier) and constrain the model to a strict allow-list of callable tools
sensitive-data-exposure: Use the OpenAI API under a Business/Enterprise agreement with zero data-retention and no-training terms rather than consumer ChatGPT for corporate data
Redact or tokenise PII and secrets in a pre-processing layer before prompts are sent to the provider
Log and monitor prompt/response content in your own boundary with strict access controls rather than relying on provider-side logs
saas-data-leakage: Publish an acceptable-use policy defining what data classifications may be sent to OpenAI and enforce it with a DLP or LLM-gateway egress proxy
Route all traffic through a corporate LLM gateway that inspects, classifies, and blocks restricted data before it leaves the network
Disable or block consumer ChatGPT usage on managed devices and provide the sanctioned enterprise API endpoint instead
credential-theft: Store API keys in a secrets manager and inject at runtime; never embed keys in frontend, mobile, or client-side code
Use project-scoped API keys with the minimum necessary scope and rotate them regularly; set usage limits per key
Proxy all OpenAI calls through a backend service so the key is never exposed to end-user clients, and scan repos/CI for leaked sk- keys
excessive-permissions: Define function/tool schemas with the narrowest possible parameters and back each tool with server-side authorization checks independent of the model
Run agentic tool execution under a dedicated least-privilege service identity, not the calling user or an admin credential
Gate destructive or high-value tool calls behind explicit human approval and rate limits
injection-attack: Never render model output as trusted HTML/Markdown or pass it to eval, shell, or SQL without context-aware encoding and validation
Constrain outputs to strict JSON schemas and validate them server-side before use
Apply output encoding and a Content Security Policy when displaying model responses in a browser
third-party-integration-risk: Design for provider failure with timeouts, fallbacks, and graceful degradation, and monitor the OpenAI status page and API error rates
Review and restrict any Assistants tools, plugins, or Actions that can reach internal systems, and scope their network egress
Maintain a vendor risk assessment and contractual data-protection terms (DPA, zero-retention) for the provider

services.name: Anthropic API
services.description: Third-party hosted LLM API (Claude models via the Messages API) consumed over the internet

threatContext.prompt-injection: Jailbreaks and system-prompt extraction against the /v1/messages endpoint, indirect prompt injection from documents, tool_result blocks, or MCP server responses fed back into the conversation, malicious content in multimodal (image/PDF) inputs steering Claude tool_use decisions
threatContext.sensitive-data-exposure: Confidential data, secrets, and source code placed in Messages API prompts or system prompts and sent to Anthropic, sensitive completions logged application-side, prompt caching retaining context blocks, data leaving the org boundary unless covered by enterprise zero-retention terms
threatContext.saas-data-leakage: Regulated or proprietary data leaving the organisation in Messages API requests or batch jobs, use of the consumer Claude.ai product instead of the enterprise API for corporate data, document uploads sent to a third-party processor
threatContext.credential-theft: Anthropic API keys (sk-ant-...) leaked in client-side code, mobile apps, public repos, or CI logs, workspace/admin keys with broad scope reused across services, keys exposed in browser-facing frontends
threatContext.excessive-permissions: tool_use definitions exposing high-privilege actions the model can invoke autonomously, agentic loops and MCP tool servers acting without human confirmation, computer-use / bash tools granting broad system access, overly broad tool input schemas
threatContext.injection-attack: Insecure handling of Claude output rendered as HTML/Markdown (stored XSS), passed to eval/exec, used in SQL, or executed as shell/code without validation (OWASP LLM02), unvalidated tool_use arguments driving downstream commands
threatContext.third-party-integration-risk: Reliance on a single external provider for availability and confidentiality, provider-side breaches or model deprecations affecting the application, MCP connectors and tools reaching internal systems and data sources

prompt-injection: Keep system prompts separate from untrusted user and retrieved content, and wrap external documents in clearly delimited, untrusted-content blocks rather than merging them into instructions
Require human confirmation for any tool_use call that changes state or performs high-impact actions, and constrain Claude to a vetted allow-list of tools
Apply input/output screening (moderation or a classifier pass) and validate tool_use arguments before executing them
sensitive-data-exposure: Use the Anthropic API under a commercial/enterprise agreement with zero-retention and no-training terms rather than consumer Claude.ai for corporate data
Redact or tokenise PII and secrets in a pre-processing layer before requests reach the Messages API
Keep prompt/response logging within your own boundary with strict access controls and be deliberate about what is stored in cached context blocks
saas-data-leakage: Define which data classifications may be sent to Anthropic in an acceptable-use policy and enforce it with a DLP or LLM-gateway egress proxy
Route all Messages API traffic through a corporate LLM gateway that classifies and blocks restricted data before egress
Block consumer Claude.ai usage on managed devices and provide the sanctioned enterprise API endpoint instead
credential-theft: Store sk-ant- keys in a secrets manager and inject at runtime; never embed them in frontend, mobile, or client-side code
Use workspace-scoped keys with least privilege, set spend limits, and rotate keys regularly
Proxy all Anthropic calls through a backend so keys are never exposed to clients, and scan repos and CI logs for leaked keys
excessive-permissions: Define tool_use schemas with the narrowest parameters and enforce server-side authorization on every tool independently of the model
Run agentic, computer-use, and MCP tool execution under a dedicated least-privilege identity in a sandboxed environment
Require explicit human approval and rate limits for destructive or high-value tool calls
injection-attack: Never render Claude output as trusted HTML/Markdown or pass it to eval, shell, or SQL without context-aware encoding and validation
Constrain responses to strict JSON schemas (or tool_use structured output) and validate them server-side before acting
Apply output encoding and a Content Security Policy when displaying responses in a browser
third-party-integration-risk: Design for provider failure with timeouts, fallbacks, and model-version pinning, and monitor Anthropic status and API error rates
Review and scope any MCP connectors or tools that reach internal systems, restricting their network egress and data access
Maintain a vendor risk assessment and data-protection terms (DPA, zero-retention) with the provider
